summary: This Dockerfile creates a minimal container based on Alpine Linux, copies a shell script into it, makes that script executable, and then runs a command that keeps the container alive indefinitely without doing anything. It's a common pattern for creating a container that you can exec into to run the script manually.

explanations.3: COPY takes a file from your computer (counter.sh) and places it inside the container's filesystem at the root level, also named counter.sh.
explanations.5: chmod +x makes the counter.sh file executable — it adds permission to run it as a program rather than just reading it as text.
explanations.7: This runs 'tail -f /dev/null', which tails an empty file and follows it forever, keeping the container running without consuming resources; it's a no-op that prevents the container from exiting.
